name: Dermamelan
lead: Dermamelan is the name of a depigmenting (skin-lightening) treatment marketed for melasma and other pigmentation, described in the literature as a non-hydroquinone bleaching formulation [1]. It is a professional aesthetic treatment rather than a chemical peel in the classical sense, and it is discussed in appearance communities as a way to even out skin tone.

Published evidence is very thin. A pilot study published in 2011 used reflectance confocal microscopy, an in vivo imaging technique, to assess the efficacy and safety of a new non-hydroquinone formulation called Dermamelan for melasma, motivated by the observation that treatment of melasma with the common agent hydroquinone remains unsatisfactory [1]. No larger trials appear among the available sources.

paras: One pilot study, published in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology in 2011, evaluated Dermamelan as a novel non-hydroquinone bleaching agent for melasma, using standard assessments plus reflectance confocal microscopy to examine the skin in vivo [1]. The study is described by its authors as a pilot, and the available abstract text does not allow further detail on sample size or outcomes to be reported here. No other published trials were identified.

Melasma is a common pigmentary disorder caused by abnormal melanin deposits in the skin, and hydroquinone is currently the most popular depigmenting agent, although treatment results are described as unsatisfactory, creating interest in alternatives [1].

timeline.event: Pilot study of the Dermamelan formulation for melasma using reflectance confocal microscopy published [1].

refs.title: A pilot study using reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM) in the assessment of a novel formulation for the treatment of melasma

card.summary: A professional non-hydroquinone depigmenting treatment for melasma, backed by one small pilot study.
card.note: Only a single 2011 pilot study was found; depigmenting treatments can cause irritation and should be professionally supervised according to dermatology guidance generally.

quick.overview:
Dermamelan is a depigmenting treatment marketed for melasma and uneven pigmentation. It is described in the literature as a non-hydroquinone bleaching formulation.

The published evidence is limited to one small pilot study from 2011 that used confocal microscopy to examine the skin.
quick.mechanism: It is intended to reduce melanin deposits in the skin; the available source describes it as an alternative to hydroquinone, the most widely used depigmenting agent.
quick.risks: Safety was assessed in the pilot study, but larger trials have not been identified, so the full adverse-effect profile is not documented in the sources reviewed.
